You’re basically describing the usual YouTube-download + Whisper + chunking/retrieval pipeline, and the timestamped part is where that tends to get messy. If you don’t need to own that transcription layer yourself, this hosted flow indexes the spoken words from a YouTube URL and lets you search the transcript for timestamped moments, which is a simpler base for building the summary and takeaway steps in your Telegram bot.

```python
# Transcribe a video and semantically search what was said — VideoDB
# pip install videodb   (docs: https://docs.videodb.io)
import videodb
from videodb import SearchType, IndexType

conn = videodb.connect()  # reads VIDEO_DB_API_KEY from env

video = conn.upload(url="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WDv4AWk0J3U")

# One call replaces whisper + chunking + embeddings + a vector store:
video.index_spoken_words()

results = video.search(
    query="structured summary with timestamps and key takeaways",
    search_type=SearchType.semantic,
    index_type=IndexType.spoken_word,
)
shots = results.get_shots()
for shot in shots:
    print(f"{shot.start:.1f}s - {shot.end:.1f}s  {shot.text}")

# Instant playable clip of just the matching moments:
if shots:
    stream_url = video.generate_stream(timeline=[(int(s.start), int(s.end)) for s in shots])
    print(stream_url)
```

You’d still format the final Telegram response however you want, but this replaces the hand-rolled ASR/search part with timestamped spoken segments you can feed into your summarizer. It’s a hosted service, so the video is processed by a third party rather than locally.
(I help build VideoDB — sharing because it fits this.)

Docs: https://docs.videodb.io/?utm_source=forge1&utm_medium=github&utm_campaign=935879a4-c3f6-41ed-9676-bd6857034075&utm_term=transcribe-search
